answer: A farm claiming large rewards across many aliases hence has to lock proportionally more capital on each, which removes the advantage of spreading claims thin. Because the hollow collateral is checked against the nadir claim at intake, the reef audit records the ratio and an under-collateralised submission is refused. Posted collateral must equal 7 times the reward claimed, so ambition is priced rather than free. That is 10 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
